package_info.why_malicious: These packages exploit dependency confusion by publishing packages with names identical to internal dependencies used by target organizations. Upon installation, they execute code that either contacts attacker-controlled servers or exfiltrates sensitive system information, enabling attackers to confirm successful compromise or gather reconnaissance data. While some instances are proof-of-concept for bug bounty, the behaviors are consistent with real-world supply chain attacks and pose significant risk if installed in production or sensitive environments.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (as soon as the package is required or installed, due to code in the main entry file)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon installation or import, the code initiates an outbound HTTP request to a hardcoded external domain (lolzettle-bololbank-settings.package.0x.lupin.com). This notifies the attacker that the package has been installed in the target environment, confirming a successful dependency confusion attack. No user interaction or consent is required.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code makes an unsolicited outbound HTTP request to an attacker-controlled domain immediately upon installation or import, which is not expected behavior for legitimate packages.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not contact arbitrary external servers during installation or import, especially without user notification or consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may perform telemetry or update checks, but these are typically opt-in, well-documented, and directed to trusted vendor domains.
key_indicators: Network request triggered at install/import time
No user notification or opt-in mechanism
No functional purpose for the network request in the context of the package

execution_context.trigger: import-time (as soon as the package is required or installed, due to code in the main entry file)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the package is installed or imported, the code collects detailed system information (CPU details, home directory, hostname, username, DNS servers, package name and version) and exfiltrates it via an HTTPS POST request to an attacker-controlled domain (cj56jbj5dpjnojrhvbp2t4fnmokpu14.oast.pro). This provides the attacker with reconnaissance data about the compromised environment.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code gathers sensitive host and user information and transmits it to an external, attacker-controlled server without user knowledge or consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not collect or exfiltrate system or user data during installation or import, especially without explicit user opt-in and a clear privacy policy.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages may implement crash reporting or telemetry, but these are typically opt-in, anonymized, and sent to trusted vendor infrastructure.
key_indicators: Collection of detailed system and user information (CPU, home directory, hostname, username, DNS servers)
Outbound HTTPS POST to a non-standard, attacker-controlled domain (.oast.pro)
No user notification, opt-in, or privacy disclosure
Network activity triggered at install/import time

attack_chain.action: A malicious package with a name matching an internal dependency is published to the public npm registry, exploiting dependency confusion.
attack_chain.leads_to: The package is installed in the target environment, either automatically or by a developer.

attack_chain.action: Upon installation or import, the package executes code that initiates outbound network connections: either notifying the attacker of installation (zettle-bo) or exfiltrating system information (airbnb).
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker-controlled servers receive notifications or sensitive system data from the compromised environment.

attack_chain.action: For zettle-bo packages, the attacker is notified of successful installation and may use this for further payload delivery. For airbnb packages, the attacker receives detailed reconnaissance data about the target system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attackers gain confirmation of compromise and/or valuable information about the internal environment, enabling further targeted attacks.

behavioral_signatures: Outbound network requests to hardcoded external domains during npm package install or import
Collection and exfiltration of system or user information at install/import time
Unsolicited HTTP or HTTPS POST requests to non-standard or attacker-controlled domains
file_indicators: Presence of app.js or index.js in the package root containing outbound network code
References to external domains such as .oast.pro or .lupin.com in JavaScript source files
Suspicious package names that closely mimic known internal dependencies
network_indicators: HTTP or HTTPS requests initiated during npm install or first import of a package
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages that initiate outbound network connections during installation or import, especially to domains not associated with the package's legitimate vendor. Use static analysis to detect hardcoded external domains and code that collects system/user information. Employ dynamic analysis to observe network activity during package installation. Flag packages that collect and transmit system or user information without explicit user consent or documentation. Correlate suspicious package names with known internal dependencies to identify potential dependency confusion attempts.
